Title: Tom W
Review_Text: So I can now say I’ve been in the tallest building in the world. You have two options. You can go up to the 124th/125th floors (costs about £30) or choose to go up to the 148th floor (cost about £80). We decided on the later. For this price you also get a fast pass (so not much queuing) and refreshments. We went during Ramadan, so refreshments weren’t available. If you do decide to go to the 148th floor, you can then come down and look at the views from the 124th/125th floors. We did this and must admit, you can’t tell any difference from looking down from the 124th compared to the 148th. The views are exactly the same. It’s like looking out of a plane window at 10,000ft compared to 15,000ft, you wouldn’t know the difference unless someone told you what height you were flying at. All you can see is, it’s a long way down to the ground. And because of this, I would only recommend going to the 124th/125th floors, this way you will also save yourselves a lot of money.

Review_Text: Fantastic building but best viewed from the outside. From the moment we arrived it was unpleasant and chaotic. Appears to be everyone for themselves to get to the top but then it all stops as you join the variety of queues, for photos which can’t be bypassed, a souvenirs shop which has poor lighting, insufficient air conditioning and staff.Then the fun begins with a 45 minute queue to get back down to reception so we could be escorted by one of the staff through a variety of fire exits and back of house corridors to get into another lift to the 3rd floor for the roof top dining. The dining experience by the pool and the view of the outside of the building was a relief but our overall experience was unpleasant and unsafe, so glad we didn’t bring the kids. Certainly designed for maximum commercial gain and not customer focused.A lot of lessons couldn’t be learned by the management if the visited the Empire State building in New York or the Titanic experience in Ireland. This is an honest review, please take care of the health and safety of your staff and customers as this is an accident waiting to happen.
